packages.title: UK ETS 2026 country-specific factor list 24 July QA
facts: UK ETS technical guidance lists 2026 carbon emission factors for annual emissions reporting with a 24 July 2026 guidance update.
The country-specific factor list is tied to UK ETS monitoring and reporting.
The Monitoring and Reporting Regulation allows nationally reported data to be used as default factors in specific circumstances.
The factors draw on UK Greenhouse Gas Inventory data.
A default factor is not itself monitored installation activity or a parcel measurement.

packages.title: UK ETS default-factor scope QA
facts: UK ETS default factors are permitted only in specified monitoring and reporting circumstances.
Use of a factor does not remove the need for the relevant activity quantity.
Factors and activity data must retain their units and reporting period.
A factor cannot be relabelled as a verified emissions total without calculation and scheme controls.
No factor is assigned directly to a parcel.

packages.title: UK ETS calorific-value separation QA
facts: The 2026 UK ETS country-specific material includes calorific values as well as carbon emission factors.
Calorific value is an energy-content parameter rather than an emissions total.
Carbon factors and calorific values must not be interchanged.
The applicable fuel and reporting basis must be preserved.
No calorific value is treated as parcel CO2e.

packages.title: UK ETS factor-vintage QA
facts: The factor list is explicitly for annual emissions reporting in 2026.
Earlier-year factor tables remain separately available.
Reporting-year vintage must be retained when factors are used.
A 2026 factor must not silently replace a factor required for another reporting year.
No cross-year factor mixing is accepted without explicit methodology.

packages.title: UK ETS waste Q2 reporting-template QA
facts: UK ETS technical guidance provides a revised Waste Quarterly Data Report template for quarter 2.
The template is intended for waste operators in the voluntary monitoring reporting and verification period.
A reporting template is a data-collection instrument rather than verified annual emissions evidence.
Quarterly waste reporting must remain distinct from annual surrender obligations.
No parcel emissions are inferred from template availability.

packages.title: UK ETS voluntary waste MRV QA
facts: Waste operators referenced by the Q2 template are participating in a voluntary monitoring reporting and verification period.
Voluntary MRV status is not the same as full scheme compliance status.
Quarterly reported activity must not be treated as final verified annual emissions.
Waste-sector reporting scope must be preserved separately from other UK ETS sectors.
No facility-to-parcel equivalence is assumed.

packages.title: UK ETS factor versus measurement QA
facts: An emission factor converts suitable activity data into an emissions estimate under a defined methodology.
A factor alone is not a measured mass of greenhouse gas.
Verified emissions depend on the approved monitoring approach and underlying data.
Inventory-derived defaults must retain their scheme context.
No unsupported measured-emissions claim is produced.

packages.title: NAEI by-source versus end-user QA
facts: NAEI produces UK emissions datasets on both by-source and end-user bases.
By-source attributes emissions to the sector that emits them directly.
End-user reallocates certain emissions from fuel producers to fuel users.
The two accounting views are not interchangeable.
Neither national accounting view is a parcel measurement.

packages.title: NAEI international-submission basis QA
facts: NAEI states international emissions submissions use the by-source basis.
UK greenhouse-gas data support UNFCCC reporting obligations.
Air-quality data support UNECE and related reporting obligations.
International reporting basis must be preserved when comparing datasets.
End-user reallocations must not be substituted into by-source submissions.

packages.title: NAEI devolved air-pollutant scope QA
facts: Devolved Government air-pollutant inventories use UK territorial coverage rules.
The devolved air-pollutant inventory excludes Crown Dependencies and Overseas Territories.
Figures are presented on a by-source basis unless stated otherwise.
Devolved-country totals are not equivalent to UK totals.
No local parcel value is inferred from devolved inventory totals.

packages.title: NAEI offshore unallocated-source QA
facts: NAEI states offshore oil and gas exploration and production sources are not allocated to an individual devolved country in the air-pollutant inventory.
These sources are reported in an Unallocated category.
Unallocated inventory emissions must not be forced into a country total without the published method.
Offshore source geography is not a cadastral parcel boundary.
No parcel assignment is made.

packages.title: NAEI international aviation and shipping QA
facts: The devolved air-pollutant reports present estimates for international aviation and shipping.
NAEI notes these are excluded from national inventory data under UNECE reporting protocols.
Presented supplementary estimates must remain distinct from the national inventory total.
Aviation and shipping scope cannot be silently merged into domestic totals.
No airport or port parcel allocation is inferred.

packages.title: NAEI air-pollutant versus GHG QA
facts: NAEI maintains separate air-pollutant and greenhouse-gas data products.
Air-quality pollutants and greenhouse gases have different reporting frameworks and metrics.
A pollutant mass cannot be relabelled CO2e without a defined greenhouse-gas methodology.
Inventory product type must be retained in downstream use.
No cross-pollutant arithmetic is performed.

packages.title: NAEI historical versus projected data QA
facts: NAEI lists 2026 historical air-quality emissions data covering 1990 to 2024.
NAEI separately lists projected air-quality emissions for 2025 to 2050.
Historical inventory data and projections have different evidential status.
Projected values must not be presented as observed emissions.
Projection uncertainty is not converted into parcel certainty.

packages.title: NAEI point and gridded-data vintage QA
facts: NAEI publishes point-source and gridded emissions products with explicit data vintages.
Spatial inventory products may lag the latest national totals.
Point-source data and gridded estimates have different spatial semantics.
A grid cell is not automatically a cadastral parcel.
Spatial vintage must be checked before joins.

packages.title: Air-quality concentration versus emissions QA
facts: Defra air-quality statistics describe concentrations of major pollutants measured across the UK.
Concentration is an ambient-air measurement and is not the same as emissions released by a source.
Concentration trends cannot be directly converted into source emission totals.
Air-quality statistics and emissions inventories must remain separated.
No parcel emission is inferred from a monitoring concentration.

packages.title: AURN monitoring-network QA
facts: Defra states the Automatic Urban and Rural Network is the UK's highest-quality network of air-quality monitoring stations.
AURN supplies monitoring data used in the annual air-quality statistics.
Station observations represent monitoring locations rather than all land parcels.
Network concentration data require spatial interpretation before local use.
No station value is copied to a parcel without evidence.

packages.title: PM2.5 concentration-metric QA
facts: Defra reports particulate matter concentrations for PM10 and PM2.5.
PM classifications are based on aerodynamic particle size.
PM2.5 concentration statistics are air-quality exposure indicators rather than greenhouse-gas totals.
Mass concentration units must not be mixed with emissions inventory units.
No CO2e conversion is inferred.

packages.title: DfT domestic transport 110.4 MtCO2e QA
facts: DfT reports domestic transport greenhouse-gas emissions of 110.4 MtCO2e in 2024.
The value was similar to 2023, when the release reports 110.2 MtCO2e.
The statistic is UK domestic transport in scope.
A national modal-sector total is not a parcel measurement.
The 2024 reference year must be preserved.

packages.title: DfT domestic transport 30 percent share QA
facts: DfT reports domestic transport accounted for 30% of total domestic UK greenhouse-gas emissions in 2024.
The percentage is a share of domestic GHG emissions, not a share of all environmental impacts.
The denominator must remain the published domestic GHG total.
The sector share cannot be assigned uniformly to locations.
No parcel percentage is inferred.
